text:
alex: ran the 4-way quant bakeoff on new-xl-3B (baseline FP16). quick summary: AWQ best perf/cost tradeoff but two layers blow up on openqa (EM drop ~9pts). GPTQ keeps accuracy but higher latency. INT8 fast but large quality regression on long-context. FP8 unstable without per-channel rescale.
mira: can you paste the per-layer deltas?
alex: here — small table from the run: 
```
layer, em_delta_awq, em_delta_gptq, em_delta_int8
12, -0.2, +0.1, -1.0
23, -8.9, -0.5, -6.7
34, -0.3, +0.0, -0.9
```
layer 23 is the culprit across AWQ/INT8. GPTQ had a partial mitigation but slower.
sam: did you run the outlier-channel scan?
alex: yes. top offending channels in layer 23: [102,103,121,129,130]. activation histogram has heavy tails. dump attached to the experiment run (s3://redwood-ml/qa/bakeoff/1907654321/outlier-layer23.json).
jen: any quick mitigations that don't require full re-quant?
alex: tried two cheap ops: 1) surgical skip for layer 23 (keep FP16), 2) per-channel clamp for top 5 channels at 3 sigma. results: skip -> EM recovers +8.5 (near baseline) and latency cost +2%. clamp -> EM +4.0 but fully quantized.
mira: interesting. so tradeoff is small latency hit vs full quant. which one does product prefer?
sam: product will prefer predictable latency bump if accuracy matters. but we should also test fallback routing: host AWQ by default, fallback to GPTQ for requests >1024 tokens?
alex: did a quick routing sim: high-TTL long ctx routed to GPTQ reduces tail errors but increases p99 latency by ~40ms. need ops input for SLA impact.
quant-bot: [auto-report] bakeoff 1907654321: AWQ median perf 18ms/token, GPTQ 28ms/token, INT8 14ms/token. noted layer 23 outliers. artifacts uploaded.
ops-bot: tagging @platform — can we add a canary with surgical-skip config to dedicated dev pool?
mira: config snippet I recommended for canary (keeps everything quantized except layer 23):
```
quant_config:
  mode: awq
  per_channel_clamp: true
  surgical_skip_layers: [23]
  clamp_topk_channels: []
  routing_policy:
    default: awq
    long_context: gptq
```
jen: let's also add telemetry: token-level accuracy drift and model-version compare on canary to catch regressions.
alex: agreed. action items:
- alex: run full eval suite with surgical-skip and clamp variants (end of day)
- mira: spin canary on dev dedicated pool + telemetry (ETA tomorrow)
- sam: confirm product SLA tolerance for +2-5% latency (today)
- jen: add regression alert thresholds to the rollout plan
mira: thanks — will update the bakeoff doc and link the canary once deployed. :thumbsup:
